stories.title: Anthropic's shares open 34% above their IPO price, valuing it at about $2 trillion
stories.summary: Anthropic's shares opened at $111.50 in their Nasdaq debut on 19 November, 34% above the $83 IPO price, valuing the maker of Claude at around $2 trillion, per The Register and Reuters.

predictions.note: A frontier AI lab, Anthropic, was valued at about $2 trillion at its first trade on the Nasdaq.

stories.title: At the opening bell, Dario Amodei pledges to pace AI so it stays under human control
stories.summary: In his Nasdaq opening-bell speech, Anthropic's CEO said 'we will pace the training and deployment of AI systems', taking as long as needed to be confident they are safe and stay under human control. He began with his father, who died of a disease that became curable a few years later.

stories.title: Trump tells APEC the US leads the world in superintelligence and opposes global rules on it
stories.summary: Speaking to the APEC leaders' meeting in Shenzhen, President Trump called the US 'the world leader in superintelligence', said it is 'almost completely good, but it's got some bad elements', and said the US opposes 'any form of globalist regulation' to control or stifle it, per ANI.

predictions.note: The US president told APEC leaders the US opposes any form of globalist regulation to control or stifle superintelligence.
The US rejected global rules for superintelligence in front of Asia-Pacific leaders, a setback for a multilateral framework.

stories.title: South Korea's exports pass $1 trillion this year on the AI chip boom
stories.summary: South Korea's exports so far this year exceeded $1 trillion as of 19 November, driven by the AI chip boom, making it the fourth country to reach the milestone after the US, China and Germany.

stories.title: Alibaba is training its next Qwen model on its own chips as US curbs tighten
stories.summary: Alibaba CEO Eddie Wu said on its earnings call that the company is training the next generation of its flagship Qwen model on its own T-Head chips, and that after 2027 most of its new AI chip supply should be its own.

stories.title: Nvidia's headhunters reportedly approach Arm boss Rene Haas to succeed Jensen Huang
stories.summary: Heidrick & Struggles, the search firm hired by Nvidia's board, has reportedly approached Arm CEO Rene Haas, who spent seven years at Nvidia, as it looks for Jensen Huang's successor, according to Bloomberg.

stories.title: ChatGPT's Live Dictation now types as you speak, with no 10-minute limit
stories.summary: OpenAI updated ChatGPT's Live Dictation so transcribed words appear in real time as you talk, and removed the previous 10-minute recording limit.

stories.title: Merck and Isomorphic Labs team up to design cancer drug candidates with AI
stories.summary: Merck and Isomorphic Labs, the AI drug-design company led by Demis Hassabis, announced a research collaboration to discover small-molecule candidates against a cancer target, with Merck running any clinical development. No candidate has been tested in people yet.

predictions.note: A major drugmaker signed on to have Isomorphic's AI design cancer drug candidates; none has reached human trials yet.

stories.title: Britain's first brain-implant centre, in Newcastle, gets more than £6m to grow
stories.summary: The National Centre for Neurotechnology and Neurorestoration in Newcastle, the UK's first centre dedicated to brain implant technology, secured more than £6m to expand treatments, recruit staff and grow its facilities.

stories.title: The European Commission confirms an AI-assisted cyberattack hit it last month
stories.summary: The European Commission confirmed it was hit by what it called an 'AI-generated cyber campaign', first detected on 22 October. Politico reported the attackers used the open-source AI hacking platform ARTEX, and staff systems such as payroll were reportedly disrupted.

stories.title: Meta's emissions jump 45% as it builds for AI; it is re-evaluating its 2030 net-zero goal
stories.summary: Meta's 2026 sustainability report shows its emissions rose 45% and its electricity use 35% in a year as it expanded AI infrastructure, and executives said they are 're-evaluating' its 2030 net-zero goal.

predictions.note: Meta's AI build-out raised its electricity use 35% and pushed it to reconsider its climate goal, and it may use gas plants.

stories.title: Google picks Blue Origin's New Glenn to launch its AI server satellites in early 2029
stories.summary: Google and Blue Origin announced that New Glenn will launch Project Suncatcher satellites carrying Google's TPUs into orbit in the first quarter of 2029, with computing capacity at roughly the scale of a data center rack.

predictions.note: Google's next orbital-compute step is a rack-scale launch planned for 2029, so its orbital AI chips stay at demonstrator scale for now.
Google booked a dedicated heavy-lift launch for satellites carrying a data center rack's worth of AI chips.

stories.title: Musk says Tesla plans a Model Y with no steering wheel or pedals, for six or seven riders
stories.summary: At the DealBook Summit, Elon Musk said Tesla plans an autonomous Model Y without a steering wheel or pedals, sized for six or seven people. He gave no date or price.

stories.title: Science Corp raises $400 million for an eye implant that restores reading vision
stories.summary: Science Corp, founded by former Neuralink president Max Hodak, raised a $400 million Series D for PRIMA, a tiny implant under the retina that restores reading vision in some people blinded by late-stage macular degeneration and is CE-marked in Europe.

predictions.note: A CE-marked retinal implant that restores reading vision raised $400 million to expand in Europe and seek US approval.

stories.title: Canva adds a switch to turn off most of its generative AI
stories.summary: Canva now lets users turn off most of its generative AI features in their settings, and a second setting shows less AI-generated content.

transcript.t: Welcome to the Singularity Daily, Friday edition.
Here's your day in superintelligence, in 3 minutes flat.
Anthropic went public today, and its shares opened at $111.50, up 34%.
At that price, Claude's maker is worth about $2 trillion.
At the opening bell, its boss Dario Amodei promised to pace AI and keep it under human control.
He started with his dad, who died of a disease that became curable just a few years later.
In Shenzhen, President Trump told Asia-Pacific leaders America leads the world in superintelligence.
His take: "It's almost completely good, but it's got some bad elements."
South Korea's exports just passed $1 trillion this year, on the back of AI chips.
Over in China, Alibaba says it's training its next Qwen model on its own chips.
And Nvidia's headhunters have reportedly approached Arm's boss, Rene Haas, about replacing Jensen Huang.
Oh, and ChatGPT now types your words as you say them, with no 10-minute limit.
Merck teamed up with Isomorphic Labs, Demis Hassabis's drug company, to design cancer drug candidates with AI.
And Britain's first brain implant centre, in Newcastle, just got over £6 million to grow.
The catch? The European Commission says hackers used AI to attack it last month.
Meta's emissions jumped 45%. Now it's rethinking its climate goal.
So... is it so over?
We're so back!
Google picked Blue Origin's New Glenn rocket to launch its AI server satellites in early 2029.
Elon Musk says Tesla plans a Model Y with no steering wheel, for six or seven riders.
Science Corp raised $400 million for an eye implant that helps some blind people read.
Superintelligence is going public. So the public should get a say.
Every day, the curve gets a little steeper.
And the future keeps arriving ahead of schedule.
One day, all of this. Tomorrow, probably more.
That's the Singularity Daily for today.
See you tomorrow.
Want the whole month? Hear more on November 27.
